subject.title: Add Herdr state bridge for OpenClaw TUI

question: Should Herdr pane-state reporting be a plugin-gated bundled integration, explicit core TUI behavior, or kept outside core until a generic TUI status seam exists?
rationale: The PR presents a bundled plugin but implements ambient core TUI behavior, and automation cannot choose the permanent product/API boundary for a Herdr-specific integration.

options.title: Gate Through Plugin Policy
options.body: Keep the bundled plugin direction, but start the sidecar only after resolved plugin activation honors global enablement, allowlist, denylist, and per-plugin disabled state.

options.title: Make It Core-Owned
options.body: Remove the misleading no-op plugin shell and document the `HERDR_PANE_ID` behavior as an explicit TUI-owned integration with maintainer-approved env controls.

options.title: Move Outside Core
options.body: Pause or close the PR unless a generic TUI status API is added that lets Herdr live as an external plugin or ClawHub package.

recommendation.title: Gate Through Plugin Policy
recommendation.body: Keep the bundled plugin direction, but start the sidecar only after resolved plugin activation honors global enablement, allowlist, denylist, and per-plugin disabled state.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses TUI lifecycle and plugin policy boundaries where recent history shows repeated ownership signals.
